caveats: AC-S7-3 adapted from per-task to group-level assertion because the Task interface has no groupId field (tasks are partitioned by group via TaskStoreProvider). Group-level is equivalent and arguably stronger (catches groups loaded with no tasks).
priorGroupIds excludes shared groups (where groupIdA === groupIdB) to avoid false positives when B was already a member of A's group.
Deliberate-regression behavioral verification for AC-S7 deferred to S8's AC-VAL-1 re-run (same pattern as S1's AC-S5-4).
Direct page.evaluate in assertS7 (lines 913-917) instead of a two-party.ts helper. Minor architectural divergence; acceptable for one-call usage.
implementation_summary: Added `lastSwitched: { context: ActorId; priorGroupIds: string[] } | null` to ModelState, initialised to null in constructor and reset() (AC-S7-1). SwCommand.run now captures A's exclusive prior group IDs before the identity switch and stores them in `m.lastSwitched` (AC-S7-2). `assertS7` now reads `__notestrTestGroups()` on the post-switch context and asserts no loaded group has an idStr in `priorGroupIds` (AC-S7-3/4). The stale comment pointing to SwCommand as the assertion location was removed (AC-S7-5). Groups shared with B (where groupIdA === groupIdB) are excluded from priorGroupIds to prevent false positives when the post-switch identity (B) legitimately loads the shared group.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The spec's reference implementation for assertS7 uses `task.groupId`, but the `Task` interface does not have a `groupId` field — the task store is per-group and tasks are scoped by which TaskStoreProvider is mounted, not by a field on the task object. This required a design adaptation: asserting at the group level via `__notestrTestGroups()` rather than per-task. Additionally, the naive implementation of priorGroupIds (including both groupIdA and groupIdB) would produce false positives when B was already a member of A's group — since after the switch (pageA now as B), B's copy of the same group loads. The fix requires excluding shared groups from priorGroupIds, which required reasoning about when groupIdA === groupIdB.
retrospective.surprised_by: The spec's `priorGroupIds` was described as capturing 'the prior identity's groupIdA/groupIdB set' — but including groupIdB in priorGroupIds would cause assertS7 to fire as a false positive on every property run where B was invited, since B's group (same idStr as A's) is legitimately loaded after the switch to B's identity.
